questions.q: What did Russ and his friend do after repeatedly telling themselves they would get on MTV?
a: They messaged an MTV executive on Twitter until he gave them a chance
They bought airtime for a music video they had already filmed
They sent demo tapes to radio stations across the country
They entered a televised talent contest in Los Angeles
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the pair kept messaging an MTV executive and eventually got their chance.

questions.q: How did Russ respond to playing a show for only 40 people?
a: He enjoyed the work itself and was inspired to write another song
He stopped touring and focused on recording in a studio
He blamed his manager for the poor promotion of the show
He gave away free merchandise to everyone in the crowd
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he loved the work and turned the small gig into inspiration for a new song.

questions.q: According to the summary, what should you do about friends and family who urge you to be realistic?
a: Ignore their doubts and keep working on what you love
Ask them to manage your career and find opportunities
Follow their advice until you start earning real money
Prove them wrong before you allow yourself to begin
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the biggest critics are often realistic loved ones, and their concerns should be silenced.

questions.q: How did Russ use his discovery about the first song on an album?
a: He released one-song albums, one per week for six months
He put his strongest track last on every record he made
He released a double album full of unreleased material
He sold his songs only at live shows for several years
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he made one-song albums weekly on TuneCore after studying bestsellers.

questions.q: What two things does the summary call the only secrets to achieving big goals?
a: Belief and hard work
Talent and good timing
Money and strong connections
Confidence and good luck
questions.why: Lesson 3 says belief matters, but you must also put in the work to grow and become great.
